profile.purpose: Manage your own account info: name, photo, email, app language, and password.
profile.flow: Everything here only affects your own account, never anyone else's.
steps: Open it from the profile menu in the top-right corner (click your name/avatar).
Update your name or profile photo under "Personal Info".
Switch the app language (Indonesian/English) under "Language".
Update your password under "Security" if needed.
profile.note: Your role can only be changed by an Admin, never by yourself.

notifications.purpose: Real-time alerts for things you need to know, like stock falling below its reorder point or a count waiting for approval.
notifications.flow: The bell icon shows a red count when there are unread notifications.
steps: Click the bell icon to see the notification list.
Click a notification to jump straight to the related page.
Mark everything read once the list gets full.
notifications.note: Notifications appear automatically; nobody has to send them by hand.

theme.purpose: Switches the app's appearance between light, dark, or your system setting.
theme.flow: Your theme choice is saved in the browser, so it stays the same next time you open the app.
steps: Open the user menu (your avatar, top-right) and pick Light, Dark, or System.
theme.note: This setting only applies to the device/browser you're currently using.

logout.purpose: The menu for opening profile settings or signing out of your account.
logout.flow: Click your name/avatar in the top-right corner to open it.
steps: Click your name/avatar in the top-right corner.
Pick "Profile Settings" to update your account info.
Pick "Sign Out" to log out - you'll get a confirmation before it actually signs you out.
logout.note: You'll need to log in again after signing out to use the app.

master-product.purpose: Every item you stock: parent products, SKU variants, units, owners, suppliers and customers.
master-product.flow: A product has one or more SKUs. Stock is always recorded in the SKU base unit; other units (Pack, Box) are conversions.
steps: Fill in Categories, Units and Owners on their tabs first.
Click "New product", enter a code and name, then write the variant attributes (e.g. color: Black, Grey; size: M, L).
Untick combinations you do not sell, then save.
Open a SKU to add its barcode and packaging units (Box = 144 Pcs).
Tick SKUs and use "Print labels" for barcode or QR labels.
master-product.note: The base unit cannot change once the SKU exists, because all stock is recorded in it.

master-warehouse.purpose: The warehouse layout: zones, aisles, racks and the bins goods live in.
master-warehouse.flow: Each warehouse gets receiving, staging, quarantine and transit bins automatically. Storage bins come from the generator or one at a time.
steps: Create a warehouse; its code prefixes every location.
Use the grid icon to generate bins in bulk, e.g. aisles 01-04, 10 racks, levels A-D.
Pick a zone or aisle to see its bin grid; the color shows how full each bin is.
Edit a bin to set capacity, allowed categories and pick order.
Pick a location and print QR labels for the racks.
master-warehouse.note: The warehouse code is locked once created because it is part of every location code.

goods-receipt.purpose: Record goods that arrive: from suppliers, production or returns, with QC results and batches.
goods-receipt.flow: A draft can change any time. On posting, goods that pass QC go to the receiving bin, rejects to quarantine, and putaway tasks are created.
steps: Click "New receipt", pick the warehouse, source, supplier and goods owner.
Scan item barcodes to add lines; scan again to add quantity.
Enter any QC failures with a reason, plus batch and expiry when asked.
Save the draft or "Post to stock" right away.
Open a receipt to attach photos, for example damaged packaging.
goods-receipt.note: Purchase prices are only visible to, and entered by, Managers and Admin/Finance.

putaway.purpose: Move goods from the receiving dock into storage bins.
putaway.flow: Each posted receipt line becomes a task. Suggested bins: one already holding the same SKU and batch, then an empty bin for the category, then the nearest one.
steps: Scan an item or tap a task in the list.
Pick a suggested bin, or scan another bin QR label.
Change the quantity to split goods over several bins.
Tap "Put away here".
putaway.note: Full bins and bins reserved for another category are refused.

pick-list.purpose: Turn sales orders into pick lists on the shortest walk.
pick-list.flow: Stock is allocated FEFO (earliest expiry first, expired skipped) or FIFO, then reserved so no other order can promise it. The walk zig-zags through the aisles.
steps: Create a sales order or receive one from POS/marketplace.
Tick orders from one warehouse and "Build pick list".
The picker opens it on a phone and scans the bin label, then the item, at each stop.
If less is on the shelf, enter the real quantity and why.
pick-list.note: A short order stays open so the rest can be allocated later.

dispatch.purpose: Check, pack and hand goods to the courier.
dispatch.flow: Picked orders wait in staging. Packing needs every item scanned; stock only leaves when the parcel is dispatched.
steps: Open "To pack" and choose an order.
Scan every item; anything not in the order, or one too many, is refused.
Enter weight, parcels and size, then "Finish packing".
On "To dispatch", enter the courier and tracking number and "Dispatch"; the delivery order opens for printing.
dispatch.note: COGS is booked automatically on dispatch.

stock-transfer.purpose: Move stock between bins in one warehouse, or ship it to another warehouse.
stock-transfer.flow: Bin moves finish at once. Between warehouses: draft, send (stock goes to the transit bin), then the destination receives. Any shortfall is held until another manager decides.
steps: Bin move: scan the source bin, pick the item, enter a quantity, scan the destination bin.
Between warehouses: a manager drafts and presses "Send".
At the destination, press "Receive" and enter what actually arrived, with a reason if short.
Another manager decides the shortfall: write off or keep in transit.
stock-transfer.note: Warehouse workers can move bin to bin; warehouse transfers are made by managers.

stock-opname.purpose: Count physical stock and correct the system with a manager's approval.
stock-opname.flow: Starting a count records system quantities and locks the bins. Counters work without seeing system quantities (blind count). A manager sees the variances and their value, then approves or rejects.
steps: Create a count: warehouse, locations or category.
Press "Start counting".
Scan each bin, enter the quantity per item, scan unexpected items.
Submit once every line is counted.
Another manager approves; stock is adjusted automatically.
stock-opname.note: Whoever submits a count cannot approve it.

stock-audit.purpose: Trace every stock move and every master data change.
stock-audit.flow: Movements cannot be edited or deleted by anyone. The stock card shows the opening balance, ins, outs and running balance per SKU.
steps: Pick a date range, SKU, type or document number.
Open "Stock card" and pick a SKU for its running balance.
"Master audit" shows who changed products, locations, access and more.
stock-audit.note: The warehouse filter in the header applies here too.

dashboard.purpose: The state of the warehouse on one screen.
dashboard.flow: Every number comes from one database call. Money only shows for people with valuation access.
steps: Pick a warehouse in the header to narrow the numbers.
Click a card to jump to its page.
Check critical stock and expiring batches every morning.
dashboard.note: The value trend fills from daily snapshots.

valuation.purpose: Inventory value, COGS, receipt price corrections and period locks.
valuation.flow: Cost is pooled per SKU and owner across warehouses. Client consignment is never an asset.
steps: Stock value tab: pick a date, method and grouping.
COGS tab: pick a date range.
Price corrections tab: enter the real price for receipts posted without one.
Period lock tab: lock the books up to a date once it is closed.
valuation.note: Only an Admin can unlock a period.

export.purpose: Download reports for the archive or to send on.
export.flow: Reports follow the warehouse filter in the header. Text a spreadsheet would run as a formula is made safe.
steps: Pick a report.
Fill in dates, SKU or count session when asked.
Click Excel or PDF.
export.note: Valuation and COGS reports need valuation access.

integration.purpose: Connect StockDesk to other systems and decide who may do what.
integration.flow: API keys are for systems that read stock or create orders. Webhooks push events out. The Users tab manages accounts and access.
steps: Create an API key with only the access it needs and copy it when shown.
Add a webhook with an https URL, pick its events and keep the secret.
Invite users, give them a role, then add access exceptions if needed.
integration.note: Keys and secrets are shown once. If lost, create a new one or rotate the secret.

worker.title: Warehouse worker
steps: Receive: create a receipt, scan items, enter batch and expiry, post it.
Putaway: scan items in receiving and store them in the suggested bin.
Pick: open a pick list, follow the route, scan bin and item at each stop.
Pack & ship: scan picked items, enter weight and courier, print the delivery order.
Count: count the assigned bins without seeing system quantities, then submit.

manager.title: Warehouse manager
steps: Morning: check the dashboard for critical stock, expiring batches and pending putaway.
Create sales orders and generate pick lists per warehouse.
Send inter-warehouse transfers and approve receiving variances.
Start counts and approve or reject their variances (never your own count).
Use the movement log and stock card when something looks off.

admin.title: Admin
steps: Price receipts and correct the ones still estimated.
Review valuation as of a date and COGS per period, FIFO against average.
Lock the books up to a closed date.
Export reports for the archive or the accountant.
Manage users, access, API keys and webhooks.
